intel.t: Ending billionaire control of politics and lowering costs, framed through faith and his record as a teacher; he calls Paxton "the most corrupt politician in Texas.".

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: Culture war positions, led by his comments defending transgender Texans, packaged as "for they/them, not you," plus his vote on a China land sale ban.

In the TPOR poll fielded October 15 to 18, he led 51 to 47 overall, with independents 66 to 28, Black voters 87 to 11, Latino voters 60 to 39 and women 54 to 47; Paxton led white voters, men, and voters without a degree.
Disclosure on October 15 and 16 that Musk was the money behind $158M routed through SLF to Texas PAC, which Talarico has turned into an anticorruption push aimed at both Paxton and Musk.
TPOR's lead for him narrowed from six points in August to four in October, with men shifting to Paxton since September.

bottom: Talarico is the best funded Senate challenger in the country and the most outspent. His campaign says it raised $64 million from July through September 2026, a record for a Senate third quarter, and more than $134 million since launch, per the Texas Tribune on October 15, 2026, https://www.texastribune.org/2026/10/15/james-talarico-64-million-fundraising-texas-senate/. It spent $67.2 million in the quarter and held $14.6 million on September 30. The campaign says 97 percent of third quarter gifts were under $100.

Against him, Elon Musk put $158 million into the Senate Leadership Fund, which moved the same amounts into a new committee called Texas PAC, per the Texas Tribune on October 15, 2026, https://www.texastribune.org/2026/10/15/elon-musk-ken-paxton-donations-senate-gop-super-pac/. Outside groups led by SLF had put more than $217 million into ads by the end of September.
Three interests combine money and a live decision:

**Small donors.** His campaign money is broad and small. The lever is his own message: ending billionaire control of politics. That is a promise he would be measured against on campaign finance votes.

intel.t: Paxton runs as the Trump aligned conservative and frames Talarico as far left; adviser Nick Maddux cites higher taxes, boys in girls' sports and defunding the police.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: Corruption: the securities case, the 2023 impeachment, his real estate, and the disclosure that left out rental income and mortgages.
White voters 60 to 38, men 50 to 47 and voters without a college degree 50 to 47 in the TPOR poll of October 15 to 18, with men moving toward him since September.
Disclosure that Musk funded $158M of the SLF rescue through Texas PAC, after Paxton spent little on his own ads all summer.
TPOR has him down 51 to 47; a Paxton internal showed him up 3, and the Tribune tracker had Talarico up 2 on October 1.

bottom: Paxton beat Sen. John Cornyn in the May 26 runoff with Donald Trump's endorsement and has been outraised more than three to one since. His campaign raised $18 million from July through September 2026, his best quarter, against Talarico's $64 million, per the Texas Tribune on October 15, 2026, https://www.texastribune.org/2026/10/15/james-talarico-64-million-fundraising-texas-senate/. The race is being carried for him by outside money, and nearly all of it traces to one man.
Four interests combine large money with a decision a Senator Paxton would hold:

**Elon Musk.** Musk gave the Senate Leadership Fund $75 million on September 9 and $83 million about two weeks later. SLF moved the same amounts into Texas PAC on the following days. Musk also gave $10 million to Lone Star Liberty PAC and nearly $90 million to his own America PAC, per the Texas Tribune on October 15, 2026, https://www.texastribune.org/2026/10/15/elon-musk-ken-paxton-donations-senate-gop-super-pac/. Tesla, SpaceX, X and the Boring Company are all based in Texas.
**Senate Republican leadership.** SLF said it would spend nearly $200 million in Texas. The ask is a seat in a 53 to 47 Senate.

D.t: James Talarico leads by 0.9 in the forecast and wins 57% of simulations. The cushion is about 93,002 votes; a one point swing is about 50,001 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +5.4 and D +7.2. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is D +2.1. Your best recent poll is New York Times/Siena at D +5.3; your worst is InsiderAdvantage at R +0.9. 30 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Travis, a projected net 311,497 votes; Harris, a projected net 305,845 votes; Dallas, a projected net 304,204 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Tarrant, D +9.7, 7.2% of the vote; Collin, D +2.7, 4.4% of the vote; Denton, D +0.2, 3.8% of the vote; Brazoria, R +8.8, 1.4% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, James Talarico runs furthest behind in Montgomery, Brazoria, Galveston. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Large counties, 68% of voters, 58 to 39, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.41 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 56 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.08 points; White voters, 61% of voters, 38 to 60, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.04 points.
The forecast's worst groups for James Talarico: Immigration voters 22 to 76, Small counties 24 to 74, Midsize counties 34 to 63. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$21.5M cash against $4.9M. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Activity: 12 campaign stops by the candidate or surrogates in 30 days.

R.t: Ken Paxton trails by 0.9 and wins 43% of simulations. Closing it takes about 46,501 voters switching sides, or 93,002 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +7.2 and R +5.4. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is D +2.1. Your best recent poll is InsiderAdvantage at R +0.9; your worst is New York Times/Siena at D +5.3. 30 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Montgomery, a projected net 93,416 votes; Parker, a projected net 44,532 votes; Smith, a projected net 31,370 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Tarrant, D +9.7, 7.2% of the vote; Collin, D +2.7, 4.4% of the vote; Denton, D +0.2, 3.8% of the vote; Brazoria, R +8.8, 1.4% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Ken Paxton runs furthest behind in Hidalgo, Cameron, El Paso. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Large counties, 68% of voters, 39 to 58, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.41 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 42 to 56, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.08 points; White voters, 61% of voters, 60 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.04 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Ken Paxton: Black voters 20 to 78, Independents 22 to 73, Health care and Social Security voters 34 to 64. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$4.9M cash against $21.5M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

media.what: On War Room, warned that Ken Paxton has a real fight against James Talarico and told Republicans to assume they are losing.
On an episode with Ron White, praised Talarico on one issue, questioned some of his positions, and said he did not know enough about Paxton; no endorsement.
The comedian voiced support for Democrat James Talarico while a guest on The Joe Rogan Experience.
Gave $158 million to Senate Leadership Fund, which routed large sums to a pro Paxton Texas PAC, plus $10 million to Lone Star Liberty PAC.
Posted on X criticizing Talarico and helped spread a false claim about his campaign absence; Talarico said he had the flu.
Called Talarico honest on the Pivot podcast, then joined him onstage in Fort Worth, short of a formal endorsement.
Appeared in a video launching the Teachers for Talarico effort.
The band endorsed Talarico on Instagram.
Hosted a Los Angeles fundraiser for Talarico with his wife.
Gave $250,000 to Lone Star Rising, a super PAC backing Talarico, plus individual contributions.
Told Megyn Kelly that if the election were held today James Talarico would beat Ken Paxton unless Republicans change the race's trajectory.
Hosted Mark Halperin and called his view that Talarico is on track to beat Paxton 'stunning', noting polls show Talarico ahead.
